cards.q: What is SNMP and over which UDP ports does it operate?
cards.a: Simple Network Management Protocol, used to monitor and configure network devices. Polls use UDP 161 and traps use UDP 162.

cards.q: What are the four components of the SNMP model?
cards.a: Manager (NMS) which polls/collects, Agent which runs on the device, MIB the data tree, and OID the address of the data, plus community/security for access.

cards.q: What does the SNMP manager do and how does it access device data?
cards.a: The manager polls the agent's MIB via OIDs to collect data.

cards.q: What are the five SNMP operations and what does each do?
cards.a: GET reads one OID, GETNEXT walks the MIB, SET changes a value, TRAP sends an alert, and INFORM sends an acknowledged alert; GET/SET/GETNEXT are Manager-to-Agent, TRAP/INFORM are Agent-to-Manager.

cards.q: Which SNMP versions use a community string and which is secure?
cards.a: v1 and v2c use community strings in clear text (weak); v3 provides authentication plus encryption.

cards.q: What are the MIB and OID in SNMP?
cards.a: MIB is the device database (data tree); an OID is the dotted address of a value in the MIB, for example 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1 is sysDescr.

cards.q: How do you walk a MIB and read a value via SNMP from the CLI?
cards.a: Use snmpget to read one OID (e.g. snmpget -v2c -c public host 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0) and snmpwalk to walk the entire tree (e.g. snmpwalk -v2c -c public host .1).

cards.q: What are the core SNMP configuration commands on a Cisco device?
cards.a: The core is snmp-server community (v1/v2c access with RO/RW), snmp-server host (trap destination), and snmp-server group/user for v3 security.

cards.q: What commands does the snmp-server host and community configuration accomplish?
cards.a: snmp-server community defines v1/v2c access (e.g. public RO, secret RW) and snmp-server host sets the trap destination with optional v3 parameters.

cards.q: How is v3 SNMP security configured?
cards.a: Create a group with a security level (e.g. snmp-server group GRP v3 priv) and a user bound to that group with auth and privacy settings (e.g. snmp-server user admin GRP v3 auth sha Pass1 priv aes 128 Pass2).

cards.q: What are the differences between SNMP v2c and v3?
cards.a: v2c uses a community string, has no authentication, no encryption, and is legacy/lab use; v3 uses no community, supports SHA/MD5 auth, AES/DES encryption, and is for production.

cards.q: What command shows SNMP status, MIB, and sessions?
cards.a: show snmp, show snmp mib, and show snmp sessions.

cards.q: A device gives no SNMP response; what is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Likely a community string problem; check with show snmp.

cards.q: No traps are received from a device; what is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Likely a host/port issue on the trap destination; check with show snmp host.

cards.q: Which UDP port do SNMP polls and traps use?
cards.a: Polling uses UDP 161 and traps use UDP 162.

cards.q: How does SNMP data get transferred and addressed?
cards.a: Data lives in the MIB (data tree) and is addressed by dotted-decimal OIDs.
